Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

original adjective

first, earliest, as it was at the start

also originally, at first, from the beginning, earliest, the original plan, initial, initially

classical

Verg. A. 1.372: prīmā repetēns ab orīgine

prīmus, prīma, prīmum

adjective

first, original

Latin calls the original state of a thing its first: going back to the very beginning is prīmā repetere ab orīgine. Originally is ā prīncipiō or prīmō.

Other words

  • ā prīncipiō — originally, from the beginning

    phrase · classical · Tac. Ann. 1.1: Urbem Rōmam ā prīncipiō rēgēs habuēre

  • 1prīstinus: long first i (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 489, s.v. prior: from the zero grade *prīs- of the comparative, as in prīscus and prīdem.

    prīstinus1, prīstina, prīstinum — original, former (of a state or condition)

    adjective · also used · classical · Caes. BG 7.54: in prīstinum statum; Nep. Timol. 1.1: in prīstinum restituere, to restore to its original state (Lewis & Short)

  • prīmigenius, prīmigenia, prīmigenium — original, first of its kind

    adjective · also used · classical · Varr. LL 6.36: verba prīmigenia, original words, from which others are formed (Lewis & Short)

    Rare: Varro, then late writers (Lewis & Short).

  • orīginālis, orīgināle — original, from the source

    adjective, third declension · also used · late Latin · Apul. M. 11.2: Cerēs … frūgum parēns orīginālis (Lewis & Short); Hier. in Gal. 3.10: orīginālēs librī, the books in their original language (Lewis & Short)

    Late Latin (Apuleius, Jerome, Macrobius), not classical.

Examples

  • Urbem Rōmam ā prīncipiō rēgēs habuēre

    the city of Rome was originally ruled by kingsTac. Ann. 1.1

  • ut nōn sōlum in prīstinum statum redīssent, sed omnium temporum dignitātem et grātiam antecessisse vidērentur

    so that they had not only been restored to their original position, but seemed to have surpassed their standing and influence at any time beforeCaes. BG 7.54

See also original, original, former, early.
